proposed_fixes.title: Queue Mouse Jump activation until its UI window is ready
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A cold-start activation may be lost because the hotkey handler launches the UI process and immediately searches for its window.
plan: Reproduce the first hotkey after a cold start and trace process/window readiness.
If confirmed, queue activation or wait for the UI window with a bounded timeout rather than returning when no window is found.
Add coverage for activation before window creation and timeout/cancellation.
verification: Verify the first hotkey opens Mouse Jump after a cold start.
Verify repeated hotkeys and failed UI launch do not hang or launch duplicate windows.

confidence.rationale: The source exposes a launch-then-enumerate sequence, but first-versus-later activation remains unconfirmed.

comment.body: Thanks for attaching the existing files; no additional files are needed. Mouse Jump starts its UI in a separate process, and the hotkey path can attempt activation immediately after launch. Could you confirm whether failure is limited to the first hotkey after PowerToys starts, or whether later hotkeys also fail after the Mouse Jump window is open? That distinction will confirm or rule out a startup-readiness race.
